handoff: Changes requested, 2 blocking loader bugs in derived-counters.ts: a deriving workflow with malformed counters: loads with it silently dropped; a YAML alias shared across outcomes maps gives one step another step's counter. Review #1's dotted-name crash is fixed; every AC is traced.

findings.title: A malformed counters: is silently dropped when the workflow derives a counter
findings.detail:
withDerivedCounters runs before the schema check and builds counters as { ...(isObj(doc.counters) ? doc.counters : {}), ...derived.counters }. Repro: loadWorkflowText('w', text, '/repo/.agents/workflows/w.yaml', 'checkout', '/repo') on `name: w / start: a / steps: { a: { check: x, timeout: 5m, outcomes: { pass: $done, fail: a } } } / counters: hello`. It returns ok:true, and the pin holds counters: { a.fail: { max: 5 } }. The same holds for counters: null or [1]. Without a deriving edge the same file is refused '/counters must be object'. This breaks AGENTS.md › Rules: 'a failing file makes the unit corrupt, never a guess'. Whether a file is refused now depends on whether it derives.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: When doc.counters is present and not a map, return { ok: true, source: null } so the schema check refuses the file. Add a test.

findings.title: Write-back mutates shared YAML alias objects: one step's edge gets another step's counter
findings.detail:
The loop at lines 38-44 rewrites doc.steps[step].outcomes in place. parseYaml resolves *alias to the same JS object. Repro: `steps: { a: { check: x, timeout: 5m, outcomes: &o { pass: $done, fail: b } }, b: { check: y, timeout: 5m, outcomes: *o } }` (with name/start). It loads ok, but in the pinned text a.fail has counter: b.fail. The declared counter a.fail is unused, and the two fail edges share one budget of 5 instead of having one each. The counting is silently wrong, which AC1 does not allow ('the pin has a counter test.fail').
Axis: standards
Suggestion: structuredClone the parsed doc before the write-back, or build each step's outcomes as a new object instead of assigning into the parsed one. Add a test with an aliased outcomes map.

findings.title: AC3's 'loop no other edge counts' half has no fixture
findings.detail:
No fixture has an agent send-back on a loop that another edge already counts, so an implementation that counted every agent send-back on any cycle would pass. The code (derive-counters.ts:89-94) is correct.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Add a case where a check's fail already counts the loop and the agent's send-back gets no counter.

findings.title: The 'every default unwritten' doctor fixture writes a max:
findings.detail:
DEFAULTS has `reject: { to: implement, max: 3 }`, so it does not show that a workflow with no counter or max at all passes doctor.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Drop the max from DEFAULTS and add it in a separate variant if needed.

findings.title: Layout-dependent assertion on the loaded workflow
findings.detail:
not.toContain('"max":3,') depends on JSON key order.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Assert on the edge object directly.

findings.title: Agent row uses reachability instead of elementaryCycles named in the slice Notes
findings.detail:
It is equivalent (a v→u path plus u→v is an elementary cycle). It departs from the plan wording but is not a bug.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: None needed.

findings.title: max: on a use route is refused at the inner step's pointer until slice 03
findings.detail:
The flattener copies a use route's max onto each flat edge, so a max: to $done there is reported at the shared step's pointer, not the use route. The slice allows this until slice 03.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Slice 03 should move the pointer and the counting to the exit.
